content.text:
**Findings**

1. High: set member IDs do not match the spec/reference implementation.  
[cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:190) hashes set members as plain `sha1(value)`, and the interop test locks that behavior in at [cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_interop_test.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_interop_test.go:109). The referenced spec says `__set` member names are the SHA-1 identifiers for the stored values, and the Rust reference implementation computes that as the Git blob hash, not raw content SHA-1: [sets.md](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta/spec/exchange-format/sets.md:22), [types.rs](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta/crates/gmeta/src/types.rs:380). That means Entire and the reference CLI will generate different member IDs for the same set value, which breaks true set interop, especially for dedupe and tombstones.

2. High: gmeta serialization commit messages are underspecified versus the spec.  
[cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/gmeta_store.go:1089) emits only `gmeta: serialize (<n> changes)`. The spec and Rust implementation expect per-change diffstat lines for normal-sized commits, with the abbreviated `changes-omitted` form only for large writes: [remotes.md](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta/spec/implementation/remotes.md:69), [serialize.rs](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta/crates/gmeta/src/serialize.rs:411). If any tooling depends on commit-message change indexing, this branch won’t interoperate.

3. Medium: push behavior is weaker than the reference workflow.  
[cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_v2.go](/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments/cmd/entire/cli/strategy/push_v2.go:426) does a single `git push` of `refs/meta/local/main:refs/meta/main` and logs a warning on failure. The spec’s remote workflow describes fetch/merge/materialize/retry behavior for non-fast-forward cases: [remotes.md](/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/gmeta/spec/implementation/remotes.md:53). For a POC that may be acceptable, but it is not fully aligned with the intended shared-writer model.

On your two questions: as of `2026-04-27`, the public site still presents `git-meta` as `spec v0.1`, so I don’t see evidence that the public spec version itself drifted since this branch started on `2026-04-09`. The branch’s bigger issue is not page drift, it’s that the implementation is still off from the detailed spec/reference behavior in the places above. Public page: https://git-meta.com/

For rebasing: `main...HEAD` is `365` commits on `main` vs `18` on this branch, and `12` of the `16` files touched here were also changed on `main`, with substantial churn in exactly the hot files this branch edits (`manual_commit_*`, `push_*`, `resume`, `committed`, `settings`, `attach`). I would not do a commit-by-commit rebase for this branch. If the work is still meant to land, the better path is a fresh forward-port onto current `main` or a small number of squash/cherry-picks, while fixing the spec mismatches above. If this is just a POC branch, I would leave it unre-based.

I also tried a focused `go test` run, but it failed in dependency/cache setup (`gitleaks.toml` packaging and missing files under `/tmp/go-mod-cache`), so I don’t have a clean test signal from this environment.
ok, then maybe just fix 1-3 and then we do a fresh port onto main next?

I’m fixing the three interop gaps on this branch directly: set member IDs, serialization commit messages, and gmeta push conflict recovery. After that I’ll run the narrowest verification I can get working in this environment so the branch is in a cleaner state before any forward-port.

I’ve isolated the code paths that need changing. The main design choice now is to make the gmeta push path reuse the same kind of fetch/merge/retry behavior as the existing custom-ref push flow, instead of bolting on a separate one-off workaround.

I’m about to edit the gmeta store and push logic. The most invasive part is the commit-message generator, because it needs to summarize logical key changes rather than raw tree-entry count; that’s the right fix if we want the branch to line up with the reference implementation instead of just changing strings.

I’ve confirmed the set-ID fix can piggyback on the repo’s existing blob-writing semantics, which is important because the spec/reference implementation treats set member IDs as Git blob IDs, not plain content hashes. I’m patching that and the commit-message diffstat logic together so the wire format changes stay internally consistent.

I’m making the file edits now. After the code change I’ll add a couple of focused tests: one to lock the set-member ID behavior to the reference implementation, and one to prove the gmeta push path can recover from a non-fast-forward against a local bare remote.
